prompt: Write a lazy initialiser that builds its value on first use and stays correct when six threads call get() at once. Complete get and isInitialised using double-checked locking.
explanation: Double-checked locking reads the volatile field once without a lock (the cheap common case), and only takes the lock when the value still looks missing. The second check inside the synchronized block is the part beginners skip: two threads can both pass the first check, and without re-checking both would call the supplier. The volatile keyword is equally load-bearing -- it stops a thread from seeing a half-published object reference, which is exactly the bug the pre-Java-5 version of this idiom was famous for.
hints: Read the volatile field into a local variable first; that local is what you return, so you only touch the volatile field once on the fast path.
Inside synchronized (lock) { ... } re-read the field and test it again before calling factory.get() -- that second test is what makes the supplier run only once.
isInitialised is just value != null; make sure it does not call get(), or checking would create the value.
